what_its_for: Momelotinib is used to treat a disease called myelofibrosis, which is a type of bone marrow cancer that causes your bone marrow to form scar tissue. This medicine helps reduce the size of an enlarged spleen, ease symptoms like fatigue, night sweats, and bone pain, and can also help with anemia (low red blood cell counts) that is common with this disease. It is used in adults who have already been treated with another medicine for myelofibrosis.
how_to_take: Take momelotinib by mouth as a tablet, once daily with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, split, or chew it. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking your dose, do not take another dose that day — just wait and take your next scheduled dose.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 200 mg (one tablet) taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects or certain health conditions, such as kidney problems. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed and do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose at the usual time. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store momelotinib tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Store away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it may increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid taking herbal supplements like St. John's Wort, as they can make the medicine less effective. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because many medications can interact with momelotinib. Avoid live vaccines while on this medicine unless your doctor approves. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: signs of serious infection such as fever, chills, or unusual tiredness; bleeding that won't stop or unusual bruising; sudden or severe headache, vision changes, confusion, weakness on one side of the body, or trouble speaking (these could be signs of a stroke or blood clot); severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); shortness of breath or rapid heartbeat; numbness, tingling, or pain in your hands or feet (nerve problems); or skin rash, blistering, or peeling. Also contact your doctor if you feel dizzy or develop high blood pressure.
when_it_works: Momelotinib may start to ease your symptoms within a few weeks, but it can take up to 3 to 6 months to see the full benefit, including improvements in spleen size and anemia. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you do not feel different right away. Stopping suddenly can cause serious withdrawal symptoms including fever and low blood pressure.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if you are pregnant. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Kidney problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe kidney disease. Liver problems: Use with caution in patients with liver problems; your doctor will monitor you closely. Older adults (65 and older): No special dose change is needed based on age alone, but older patients may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored carefully.
